newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says Russian arms lag far behind West.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Russian arms lag far behind West.

text.p: Russia's struggling armed forces are technologically lagging far behind other leading nations, President Boris Yeltsin said in a written state of the nation address obtained by Reuters on Wednesday.

"The Russian armed forces are five to 10 years, sometimes up to 15 years, behind the world's most powerful armies in the general level of technical equipment," he said in the address, which will form the basis of a speech to parliament on Thursday.
The text, outlining policies for the year ahead, said Russia would cut its post-Cold War armed forces both in structure and in manpower and try to keep them up to date.
The document stressed the need to speed up the reform of the armed forces, which has stalled over arguments between civilian and military officials over who should spearhead it.

Yeltsin earlier ordered a 200,000 man reduction in the armed forces in 1997. The order has mainly affected vacant positions. Generals said they had 1.7 million men under arms before Yeltsin ordered the cut. But such is the state of the military, the Kremlin says it is not sure how many troops it has.
"Our aim is adequate defence, qualitatively new, slimmer forces armed with modern equipment and weapons," Yeltsin said.
Nevertheless the 66-year-old president seemed to back down on a promise made during last year's re-election campaign to end conscription by the year 2000.
His order to create a fully professional army in just four years has incurred criticism from the military who say Russia simply cannot affort an expensive contract army.

"Switching to contracts as a means of providing personnel for the armed forces will take place as the infrustructure necessary for their working and living is created," Yeltsin said in his address. He did not specify how long that might take.
